title: Microsoft Purview Data Map - Simply Explained

entities.name: Microsoft Purview
entities.quote: you will understand how Microsoft Perview helps an organization find, understand, protect and manage its data

entities.name: Microsoft Purview Data Map
entities.quote: PerView starts with the data map, which acts as a technical inventory of your connected data sources

entities.name: Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog
entities.quote: It outs at albums where the unified catalog comes in.

entities.name: Sensitivity labels
entities.quote: Think of a sensitivity label as a clear handling instruction attached to the information.

entities.name: Data loss prevention (DLP)
entities.quote: This brings us to data loss prevention, usually shortened to DLP.

entities.name: Data lineage
entities.quote: Pervue can show data lineage. Lineage is the trail behind a number.

entities.name: Data product
entities.quote: A data product is simply a useful group of related data put together for a business purpose.

entities.name: Data quality
entities.quote: Research often puts a price on poor data quality

entities.name: Governance domain
entities.quote: Pervue can group these products into governance domains too.

entities.name: Glossary term
entities.quote: The catalog can also use a business glossary

entities.name: Audit logs
entities.quote: An audit log records actions across supported services.

entities.name: Communication Compliance
entities.quote: Communication compliance works in a similar way

entities.name: Microsoft Entra ID
entities.quote: Entra ID for example acts like the reception desk for your company.

entities.name: Microsoft Fabric
entities.quote: open a report built from Azure or Microsoft fabric data.

quotes.text: An accessible report is not always a trusted report. That difference can save a team from building a decision around incomplete or outdated information.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Short, memorable distinction between access and trust in data.

quotes.text: A sensitivity label and DLP work together, but they do different jobs. The label identifies information and describes how it should be handled. DLP checks an action as it happens and can warn the person, block the action or record it for review.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clean explanation of how labels and DLP divide the work.

quotes.text: If you see a total in a fabric report, lineage can help show the source table it came from, the steps that changed it, and the reports or data products that now use it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes data lineage tangible with an everyday reporting example.

quotes.text: A pattern is not proof of bad intent. People can have valid reasons for unusual work, so these signals need careful review by the right people.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced reminder that risk signals require human judgment.

Find, name and trust data: data map, catalog and lineage
Classify and protect: sensitivity labels and DLP

takeaways: Microsoft Purview does not store your data; it adds rules, context and visibility around data that stays in Microsoft 365, Azure, Fabric and supported external sources.
The data map, unified catalog, glossary, lineage and data quality checks help people find data, know who owns it and judge whether it can be trusted.
Sensitivity labels, DLP, audit, retention, eDiscovery and communication compliance protect information as it moves and give responsible teams records and context when something goes wrong.
hook: Data rarely stays in one app: it is copied, exported, renamed and forgotten across Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Fabric. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins, data owners and compliance teams who need a plain-English map of Microsoft Purview. You learn how its data map, catalog, labels, DLP and investigation tools fit together to make data findable, trustworthy and protected.
